---
title: "dependencies & docker"
---

## what are we packaging?

- packaging brings together the fitted preprocessing/model pipeline, inference code, dependencies, and input contract
- an input contract specifies feature names or order, types, units, and allowed missing values; use it to keep predictions consistent with training
- keep a model id and the training run record beside the package so a prediction can be traced back to its source
- save preprocessing with the model and retain compatible dependency versions [scikit-learn persistence](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/model_persistence.html)

## environment and container terms

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| term / tool | definition | use case |
|---|---|---|
| virtual environment | a separate python package environment, created here with `venv` | isolate one project’s libraries |
| dependency snapshot | a file listing resolved package versions | reinstall the environment used to train the saved model |
| docker | a platform for building and running containers | package the application and its software environment |
| image / container | a packaged filesystem and configuration / an instance created from it | build once, then start instances for predictions |
| dockerfile | instructions used to build an image | specify the base image, files, installation, and startup command |
| build context | the files available to the image builder | provide the application and artifact while excluding unrelated files |
| layer / build cache | an image filesystem change / reusable build results | avoid reinstalling unchanged dependencies on every build |
| port mapping | forwarding a host port to a container port | reach the service inside the container |

:::

- an image tag is a reusable label; a digest identifies exact image content, useful when recording a reproducible release [docker build guidance](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/)

## prepare the local exercise

- [download the exercise files](../../examples/serving-demo.zip), unzip them, and open a terminal in that folder
- this uses synthetic data and python 3.12, matching the docker base image
- train and serve within the same environment before trying a container

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.in
python lifecycle_demo.py --output artifacts/run-001
python -m pip freeze > requirements-lock.txt
```

- `requirements.in` lists the required libraries; `requirements-lock.txt` records the resolved versions for this run
- this snapshot does not guarantee compatibility across operating systems or hardware, so test the resulting image

## read the dockerfile

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements-lock.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements-lock.txt
COPY --chmod=0444 app.py ./
COPY --chmod=0444 artifacts/run-001/pipeline.joblib ./artifacts/run-001/pipeline.joblib
USER 10001:10001
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

- `FROM` selects the base image, `COPY` adds files, and `RUN` executes a build step
- `USER` selects a non-root numeric user; `CMD` starts the prediction server when the container runs
- `EXPOSE` documents the container port; `-p` below actually publishes it on the host [dockerfile instructions](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-concepts/building-images/writing-a-dockerfile/)

```bash
docker build -t mlops-demo:local .
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 mlops-demo:local
```

- docker must be installed with its engine running; the host binding keeps this learning service local
- the base-image tag is convenient for the exercise; record an image digest for a fixed release
- add a `.dockerignore` to exclude the virtual environment and unrelated files from the build context
- rebuild and revalidate deliberately when updating dependencies or the model [container deployment guide](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/docker/)
